## Next move: Calculating variance!

```{python}

triplets = triplets_full[['image1','image2','image3']] - 1 #subtracting 1 so they're 0-indexed
triplets.head()

```

```{python}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Total number of responses
print(f"Total responses: {len(triplets):,}")

# Total number of unique images
unique_images = pd.unique(
    triplets[["image1", "image2", "image3"]].to_numpy().ravel()
)
print(f"Unique images: {len(unique_images):,}")

# Identify unique unordered triplets
# eg. (12, 45, 87) and (87, 12, 45) are the same triplet.
df = triplets.copy()

sorted_ids = np.sort(
    df[["image1", "image2", "image3"]].to_numpy(),
    axis=1
)

df[["id_a", "id_b", "id_c"]] = sorted_ids

# Number of unique triplets
group_cols = ["id_a", "id_b", "id_c"]

response_counts = (
    df.groupby(group_cols, sort=False)
      .size()
      .rename("n_responses")
      .reset_index()
)

print(f"Unique triplets: {len(response_counts):,}")
print(f"Mean responses per triplet: {response_counts['n_responses'].mean():.2f}")
print(f"Median responses per triplet: {response_counts['n_responses'].median():.0f}")
print(f"Minimum responses: {response_counts['n_responses'].min()}")
print(f"Maximum responses: {response_counts['n_responses'].max()}")

print("\nResponse count distribution:")
print(response_counts["n_responses"].describe(
    percentiles=[0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99]
))

```

```{python}
counts = response_counts["n_responses"]

print(f"Triplets seen once: {(counts == 1).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 2+ times: {(counts >= 2).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 3+ times: {(counts >= 3).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 4+ times: {(counts >= 4).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 5+ times: {(counts >= 5).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 10+ times: {(counts >= 10).sum():,}")
print(f"Triplets seen 20+ times: {(counts >= 20).sum():,}")

print("\nMost frequently repeated triplets:")
print(
    response_counts.nlargest(20, "n_responses")
    .to_string(index=False)
)

```

<!-- ### Variance of odd-one-out choices

Use `image3` as the selected image and group by the unordered triplet. IDs remain
**zero-indexed**. Keep the earlier threshold of 20 responses (`min_responses`).
Image IDs are categorical labels, so their numerical variance is not meaningful.
Instead, let $p_a,p_b,p_c$ be the proportions selecting each image and sum the
variances of the three binary choice indicators:

$$V = \sum_k p_k(1-p_k) = 1-(p_a^2+p_b^2+p_c^2).$$

This empirical variance (`ddof=0`, also called Gini impurity) ranges from **0**
for unanimous responses to **2/3** for an equal split. We rank and plot this
descriptive measure. The CSV also includes sample-corrected variance
$V_s=nV/(n-1)$ (`ddof=1`), which can exceed 2/3 in finite samples.
These describe variation in responses, not uncertainty in estimated proportions.
The [paper's Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.26921) discusses repeated-triplet
agreement; this analysis is not a reproduction of its consistency estimator.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

min_responses = 20
repeated_triplets = response_counts.loc[response_counts.n_responses >= min_responses]
repeated_responses = df.merge(
    repeated_triplets[group_cols], on=group_cols, how="inner", validate="many_to_one"
)
assert (repeated_responses.id_a < repeated_responses.id_b).all()
assert (repeated_responses.id_b < repeated_responses.id_c).all()
choice_cols = ["chose_a", "chose_b", "chose_c"]
for label in ("a", "b", "c"):
    repeated_responses[f"chose_{label}"] = (
        repeated_responses.image3 == repeated_responses[f"id_{label}"]
    ).astype(int)
assert (repeated_responses[choice_cols].sum(axis=1) == 1).all()
choice_counts = repeated_responses.groupby(group_cols)[choice_cols].sum().rename(
    columns={f"chose_{k}": f"n_{k}" for k in ("a", "b", "c")}
)
triplet_variances = repeated_triplets.set_index(group_cols).join(choice_counts)
for label in ("a", "b", "c"):
    p = triplet_variances[f"n_{label}"] / triplet_variances.n_responses
    triplet_variances[f"p_{label}"] = p
    triplet_variances[f"variance_{label}"] = p * (1 - p)
triplet_variances["choice_variance"] = triplet_variances[
    ["variance_a", "variance_b", "variance_c"]
].sum(axis=1)
triplet_variances["choice_variance_sample"] = (
    triplet_variances.choice_variance * triplet_variances.n_responses
    / (triplet_variances.n_responses - 1)
)
triplet_variances = triplet_variances.reset_index().sort_values(
    ["choice_variance", "n_responses", *group_cols],
    ascending=[False, False, True, True, True],
).reset_index(drop=True)
triplet_variances.insert(0, "variance_rank", triplet_variances.choice_variance.rank(
    method="min", ascending=False
).astype(int))
output_dir = Path("../data")
triplet_variances.to_csv(output_dir / "triplet_variances_20plus.csv", index=False)
top_triplets = triplet_variances.head(20)
print(triplet_variances.choice_variance.describe())
print("Highest-variance triplets (zero-indexed IDs; ties share a rank):")
print(top_triplets[["variance_rank", *group_cols, "n_responses", "n_a", "n_b", "n_c",
                    "choice_variance"]].to_string(index=False))
```

```{python}
ordered = triplet_variances.sort_values("choice_variance")
axes[0].scatter(np.arange(1, len(ordered) + 1), ordered.choice_variance,
                s=12, alpha=0.6)
axes[0].axhline(2/3, color="black", linestyle="--", label="Equal split (2/3)")
axes[0].set(xlabel="Triplet (sorited by variance)", ylabel="Empirical choice variance",
            title=f"Each triplet with {min_responses}+ responses", ylim=(0, 0.7))
axes[0].legend()
axes[1].hist(ordered.choice_variance, bins=30, edgecolor="white")
axes[1].axvline(2/3, color="black", linestyle="--")
axes[1].set(xlabel="Empirical choice variance", ylabel="Number of triplets",
            title="Distribution of choice variance")
fig.savefig(output_dir / "triplet_choice_variance_20plus.png", dpi=180)
plt.show()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 8), layout="constrained")
y = np.arange(len(top_triplets))
left = np.zeros(len(top_triplets))
for label, color in zip(("a", "b", "c"), ("#4477AA", "#EEAA33", "#228833")):
    proportions = top_triplets[f"p_{label}"].to_numpy()
    ax.barh(y, proportions, left=left, label=f"Image {label}", color=color)
    left += proportions
labels = [
    f"({int(r.id_a)}, {int(r.id_b)}, {int(r.id_c)})  n={int(r.n_responses)}  V={r.choice_variance:.5f}"
    for r in top_triplets.itertuples()
]
ax.set_yticks(y, labels)
ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), xlabel="Proportion selecting each image as odd one out",
       title="20 highest-variance triplets (zero-indexed IDs: a, b, c)")
ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.08), ncol=3)
fig.savefig(output_dir / "triplet_highest_variance_20plus.png", dpi=180)
plt.show()
```

### Save all rank-1 triplets as image strips

Read the saved rankings and use each zero-indexed image ID as a row position in
`wrangled_embeddings.csv`. Its `unique_id` column gives the corresponding JPEG
filename in `hebart_reference_images`. Panels follow `id_a`, `id_b`, `id_c` order.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image, ImageOps

# Support execution from either the project root or the models directory.
data_dir = Path("data") if Path("data/wrangled_embeddings.csv").is_file() else Path("../data")
embeddings = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "wrangled_embeddings.csv")
rank1_triplets = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "triplet_variances_20plus.csv")
rank1_triplets = rank1_triplets.loc[rank1_triplets["variance_rank"].eq(1)].copy()

low_variance_triplets = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "triplet_variances_20plus.csv")
low_variance_triplets = low_variance_triplets.nsmallest(20, "choice_variance").copy()


def save_triplet_images(
    triplet, embeddings, image_dir, save_dir, panel_size=480, gap=60, margin=10
):
    """Save one triplet as three uncropped square panels on a white PNG canvas.

    `triplet` contains zero-indexed id_a/id_b/id_c; embeddings must retain CSV order.
    Returns the saved PNG path. Requires Pillow in the notebook environment.
    """
    image_ids = [int(triplet[column]) for column in ("id_a", "id_b", "id_c")]
    if any(image_id < 0 or image_id >= len(embeddings) for image_id in image_ids):
        raise ValueError(f"Triplet IDs are outside the embeddings row range: {image_ids}")
    image_names = embeddings.iloc[image_ids]["unique_id"].tolist()
    image_paths = [Path(image_dir) / f"{name}.jpg" for name in image_names]
    for path in image_paths:
        if not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing reference image: {path}")

    canvas = Image.new(
        "RGB", (3 * panel_size + 2 * gap + 2 * margin, panel_size + 2 * margin), "white"
    )
    for position, path in enumerate(image_paths):
        with Image.open(path) as source:
            panel = ImageOps.contain(
                ImageOps.exif_transpose(source).convert("RGB"),
                (panel_size, panel_size),
                method=Image.Resampling.LANCZOS,
            )
        x = margin + position * (panel_size + gap) + (panel_size - panel.width) // 2
        y = margin + (panel_size - panel.height) // 2
        canvas.paste(panel, (x, y))

    save_dir = Path(save_dir)
    save_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    save_path = save_dir / ("triplet_" + "_".join(map(str, image_ids)) + ".png")
    canvas.save(save_path)
    return save_path


rank1_image_dir = data_dir / "triplet_photos" / "rank1"
rank1_triplets["saved_image"] = [
    str(save_triplet_images(row, embeddings, data_dir / "hebart_reference_images", rank1_image_dir))
    for _, row in rank1_triplets.iterrows()
]
print(f"Saved {len(rank1_triplets)} rank-1 triplets to {rank1_image_dir.resolve()}")
rank1_triplets[["id_a", "id_b", "id_c", "saved_image"]]
```
